searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he api architecture plan the awtsmoos renews every request before transport can pretend to be the source; awtsmoos.com will keep one calm public contract while many small domain vessels carry the force. evidence the canonical social hub already composes focused api delegates. the separate observatory still concentrates transport parsing, url construction, 32 public methods, mutation bodies, route health orchestration, and developer probes inside one api.js; its request factory is a second large switch. feedtrending exists in transport but is absent from the operation policy/groups/factory. winning architecture 1. preserve every current socialapi method and {status, ok, body} envelope. 2. split transport into route covenant, query/form vessels, response parser, structured error, and one canonical transport. 3. split methods into core, discovery, feed, profile, relationship, signal, governance, live, and developer domain clients. 4. compose those domains beneath one stable socialobservatoryapi facade. 5. replace operation arrays/switches with one immutable data only registry. 6. separate browser context adaptation (binahcontextinputresolver) from operation execution (yesodoperationexecutor). 7. generate read/mutation policy, visible groups, execution, docs, and agent catalog from that registry. 8. add a machine gateway that discovers freely, validates reads, and requires explicit allowmutation: true for mutations. 9. preserve multi group membership and existing group order. 10. make feedtrending a first class read operation. safety and compatibility unknown operations fail closed. mutation consequence text stays equivalent to the current policy. server error payloads remain intact. network failures and unreadable response bodies become structured client side errors. blank query values remain distinct from absent values. no generic agent route exposes filesystem, nodeos, or migration mutation powers. verification facade parity, exact route strings, query encoding, transport parsing, operation uniqueness, json safe catalog, mutation classification, context adaptation, agent required input errors, explicit mutation opt in, existing observatory tests, live route health probes, and browser smoke.

searchText: b"h remaining work — geelooy futuristic revelation boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos renews the instant; this ledger renews the work, so no hidden brittle edge survives beneath a polished quirk. awtsmoos.com is the visible shore; the code beneath must be equally sure. mission transform the public geelooy/ surfaces into a coherent, fast, mobile first, accessible, futuristic system while preserving real contracts and eliminating style leakage, overflow, accidental overlap, inconsistent interaction states, and tangled javascript/api boundaries. open work graph [ ] capture clean git baseline and preserve unrelated local changes. Awtsmoos.com should feel like one lucid world, though many pages carry the light unfurled. Observed Project Shape The geelooy/ root contains many distinct web fam
searchText: b"h phase one — discovery and possibility map boruch hashem. blessed is he. the awtsmoos makes each boundary new; our work must reveal what is actually true. awtsmoos.com should feel like one lucid world, though many pages carry the light unfurled. observed project shape the geelooy/ root contains many distinct web families: static information, auth, docs, apps, social/profile/heichel surfaces, editors/composers, utility tools, os style surfaces, games, apis, shared modules, and multiple existing style/script locations. ideal possibilities a consistent visual language without a single unsafe global stylesheet. page root scoped design tokens imported into each family stylesheet. small css files grouped by tokens, layout, components, state, and motion. consistent 44px+ touch targets and obvious keyboard focus. retractable navigation/panels using semantic controls and bounded overlays. responsive typography and spacing using clamp() inside safe limits. soft luminous surfaces, restrained glass effects, crisp borders, and high contrast. motion based on opacity/transform where possible, never layout thrashing spectacle. explicit prefers reduced motion fallbacks. one documented z index scale per surface; no arbitrary 999999 escalation. every flex/grid child designed with min width: 0 and overflow safe content rules. forms with clear labels, validation, errors, busy states, and password manager friendliness. data driven navigation/catalog definitions rather than duplicated markup logic. small javascript classes where lifecycle inheritance is real; composition otherwise. shared api transport with explicit request, response, error, cancellation, and parsing contracts. accessible empty/loading/error/success states across asynchronous views. documentation that explains user workflows and developer extension boundaries. browser evidence covering representative mobile and desktop routes. things we will not do no unscoped body, button, a, .card, .modal, or similarly collision prone rules. no visual rewrite that silently changes api payloads, endpoint names, auth behavior, or navigation semantics. no giant “design system” file that becomes another monolith. no decorative inheritance or mystical names that obscure technical responsibility. no global reset that breaks embedded/legacy pages. no animation without reduced motion behavior. no fixed overlay without explicit containment, close behavior, stacking contract, and mobile testing. no editing generated bundles when human authored sources exist. discovery questions to resolve from files 1. which pages already share css/js imports? 2. which html pages contain inline styles/scripts? 3. where is common navigation currently generated? 4. what api client or fetch wrappers already exist? 5. what page roots/classes are safe migration anchors? 6. which pages use fixed/sticky/absolute positioning? 7. which routes have nested local agent instructions? 8. which tests/build scripts cover browser facing surfaces? 9. which public exports and global browser names are consumed elsewhere? 10. which pages can inherit improvements through shared modules with minimal rewrites?

searchText: b"h phase two — feasibility and risk map boruch hashem. blessed is he. chesed opens possibility; gevurah gives it form. the awtsmoos renews both current and shore; awtsmoos.com must become simpler by becoming more sure. practical architecture direction styling use imported css modules, but bind every rule to an explicit page/surface root. shared modules may define reusable patterns only beneath that root contract. do not use :root tokens or generic global element selectors. each entry stylesheet becomes a manifest of @import statements for small scoped modules. layout design mobile first. use bounded content widths, min width: 0, safe wrapping, and flexible grids. fixed/sticky ui must declare its containing block and z index layer. drawers/dialogs must have a single overlay owner and deterministic close/focus behavior. interaction every actionable control receives focus visible, active, disabled, and busy semantics. hover enhancements run only on hover capable devices. motion uses bounded transform/opacity transitions and respects reduced motion. javascript prefer small classes for genuine lifecycle/state specialization and composition for services. keep public names compatible where externally consumed. introduce explicit data definitions for navigation, actions, form state, and api operation metadata instead of scattered branching. api separate request validation, transport, response normalization, error translation, and ui rendering. document every boundary. do not silently alter endpoint paths or payload contracts during ui modernization. primary risks and controls 1. style collisions — require explicit root prefix on every authored selector. 2. legacy page breakage — migrate page families incrementally and browser test representative routes. 3. hidden public globals — search call sites before renaming javascript exports/globals. 4. mobile overflow — static scan risky css and test narrow viewports. 5. overlay stacking errors — one documented z layer scale and explicit overlay ownership. 6. animation fatigue — short restrained transitions and reduced motion fallback. 7. false abstraction — extract only real responsibilities; avoid wrapper only modules. 8. huge module count without clarity — each file gets one named responsibility and obvious dependency direction. 9. api regressions — preserve contracts and test error/success paths. 10. accessibility regression — semantic controls, keyboard focus, labels, live feedback where relevant. 11. local uncommitted work — inspect git state before touching existing files and never overwrite unrelated edits. 12. generated assets mistaken for source — locate human authored source before rewrites. 13. tunnel instability — use small durable operations and verify every accepted write by readback. 14. documentation drift — docs updated from verified implementation, not aspirational behavior. migration order 1. establish evidence baseline and nested instructions. 2. inventory representative families and shared dependencies. 3. build scoped visual foundation from actual recurring patterns. 4. migrate static/info pages first to validate css isolation. 5. migrate forms/auth to validate interactive state system. 6. migrate data heavy/social/editor surfaces to validate javascript/api contracts. 7. improve docs from implemented architecture. 8. verify and then widen migration to remaining compatible families. gate no existing source rewrite begins until its full contents, callers/imports, and nearby style/runtime dependencies have been inspected.
